texts.facts: Summons could not be served upon the defendant through ordinary modes. The right of the defendant to file written statement was forfeited and defendant was proceeded against ex-parte vide order dated 28.03.2024. 3. Original Non-Starter Report dated 15.07.2023 Ex.PW1/15 Averments in the plaint 4. The Plaintiff, Bank of Baroda, is a "Scheduled Bank" within the meaning of Section 2(e) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and is also recognized under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970. The Plaintiff is a juristic entity having its Head Office at Bank Of Baroda vs Anuradha on 20 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83272389/ 3 Mandavi, Baroda, and is carrying on the business of banking through its various branches all over India, including one branch at Khureji Khas, Delhi- 110092.The plaint has been signed and verified by Mr. Vipin Kumar, who is stated to be duly authorized to do so. 5. The defendant approached the plaintiff's bank on 03.11.2021 for grant of a loan facility under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) for business of manufacturing of vegetable oil and processing units. After satisfying itself, the CS (Comm) 350/23 Date of Judgment : 20.09.2025 rv plaintiff bank sanctioned a Working Capital Cash Credit Facility of Rs. 4,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakh only) to the defendant under PMMY scheme vide loan account no. 76640500000296. 6. It is stated that in order to secure the repayment of the said facility, defendant had signed and executed various documents such as Demand Promissory Note, Letter of Sole Proprietorship, Letter of Continuing Security, Draft Undertaking, Declaration cum Undertaking cum Authority and Composite Hyphothecation Agreement. Defendant accepted the terms and conditions for repayment the loan. The rate of the interest was agreed to be paid on floating basis i.e. 7.45% per annum with monthly rests. The defendant further agreed to pay penal interest @ 2% p.a. in case of default in payment. The loan was to be repaid in 12 months subject to annual review by the plaintiff. 7. The defendant did not comply with the terms and conditions. The defendant defaulted in making payments. Consequently, the said loan account became highly irregular in terms of non-payment. Despite various reminders/letters/notices sent to the defendant for repayment of the dues but in vain. Accordingly, plaintiff issued a demand notice dated 10.05.2023 upon the defendant thereby recalling the loan agreement. The loan account of the defendant was classified as NPA on 04.04.2023 as per the guidelines of Reserve Bank of India. The defendant has paid last payment of Rs.1,000/- on 03.03.2023. The plaintiff bank also approached East District Legal Authority for pre- litigation mediation. A non starter report was issued by the authority on CS (Comm) 350/23 Date of Judgment : 20.09.2025 rv 15.07.2023. 8. The plaintiff, therefore, seeks a decree of amount Rs.4,20,872.90 (Rupees Four Lakhs Twenty Thousand Eight Hundred Seventy Two and Ninety Paise Only) alongwith pendente-lite and future interest at the rate 10.20% per annum, also 2.00% penal interest from the date of filing of suit till realization alongwith cost of the suit. Contentions of the plaintiff 9. The Ld. counsel for the plaintiff reiterated the averments contained in the plaint. He submitted that the defendant did not clear the outstanding dues. Therefore, defendant was liable to pay the outstanding dues. He prayed for interest to be awarded at the rate sought as well as for costs of the suit to be awarded to the plaintiff. Observation of the Court 10. The defendant was proceeded against ex-parte. Defendant did not file any written statement nor led any evidence on her behalf. The cash credit facility was availed by the defendant on 08.11.2021. Defendant made some payments, the last of which was made on 03.03.2023. Statement of account is maintained by the plaintiff. Despite availing the said facility, the defendant failed to make payment, thereby breaching her contractual obligations. The present suit filed on 13.09.2023, falls well within the statutory limitation period of three years and is therefore legally maintainable. This court has jurisdiction to entertain and try the suit as the loan facility was availed by the defendant and was to be repaid within the jurisdiction of this court. The plaintiff had also complied with the mandate of Section 12A of The Commercial Courts Act.
